title: feat(server): html tools take a file path, so agents stop retyping pages
author: t3dotgg
head: c183eab0a1b064d0179919f8752f8e2b6b5d65fd
body:
Agents retype the whole page every time they call `html_preview` or `html_render`, because both tools take only inline `html`. Pages often already exist as files on disk. [Discussion #23303](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/23303) measured about 30K output tokens and four minutes per copy for a 40K-character page. Agents then skip the re-preview to save time.

Now both tools also take `path` to an absolute `.html` file, and a call passes exactly one of the two. The agent writes the page once, edits the file, and passes the path.

- **File read.** The server reads the file only for full-access threads. A supervised thread gets a clear error and passes `html`, the same as before. The read uses the same guards as other disk reads: no network paths, the real path must end in `.html`/`.htm`, server-internal paths are refused, the file is opened without following links, and it must have one hard link, be at most 25 MiB, and start like an HTML document. The page is saved as a snapshot at publish time.
- **Render recovery.** ACP providers that drop tool results recover path renders by path, in publish order. A call that sends both sources published nothing, so it recovers nothing.
- **Shorter text.** Tool descriptions and agent instructions are shorter, so the agent context budget goes down.
- **Eval.** The `mcp-tool-use` eval has a new `revise-page-resends-html` case. The grader reads the file behind `path` and fails page checks when it cannot replay the file exactly. [...]

title: fix(web): snooze options line up in columns
author: SunkenInTime
head: f575c0eef46d552fd5e59b6b6a085ac3e1cf434b
body:
The snooze options in Settings → Threads didn't line up. Each row was its own wrapping flex row with the preview pushed to the right, so:

- The previews were right-aligned, so labels and times started wherever their text happened to end.
- The time fields started 20px right of the duration steppers, because "at" sat in front of them.
- When a row was too wide, its preview wrapped onto a line of its own. "In 2 days / Mon 5:38 PM" did this at the default width, and every duration row did it in a narrower window. That left gaps with a lone preview in them.

Now, when the list is at least 37rem wide, the rows share one grid (subgrid). The columns are: when, "at", amount or time, unit, preview and remove. Steppers and time fields start at the same x, every label starts at the same x, and every time ends at the same x. Below 37rem, every row puts its preview and remove button on a second line, so all rows have the same shape instead of only some wrapping.

The when and unit selects asked for `w-32` and `w-28`, but the select's `min-w-36` overrode both, so they were 144px. They now take `min-w-0` so the widths they asked for apply, which leaves room for the preview at the default width without truncating.

Red-first tests reproduce the lost wake and verify that in-turn delivery still consumes the result once.
